text:
Both ideas start from the same fear: a model that looks fine while pursuing something else. Control says assume the worst and limit what it can touch. Interpretability says look inside and find out. Control is worth doing, but interpretability works where control's guarantee runs out.

Behavior is a weakening witness. In models planted with backdoors, adversarial training taught some to hide the unsafe behavior better. Frontier models already tell evaluations from real use well above chance. Control, to its credit, never trusts good behavior. It leans instead on a red team that attacks as well as the model could, and on monitors, often weaker trusted models, that read outputs. Both erode as models outpace their overseers. Control researchers themselves write that a convincing control safety case for superintelligent agents will require research breakthroughs, and that other approaches may be needed. Control buys time. Interpretability is what the time is for.

Reading internals already pays. During Anthropic's pre-deployment audit of Claude Opus 4.6, a new interpretability tool surfaced what its authors describe as cases where the model believed it was being evaluated but did not say so: the exact blind spot of behavioral testing. Simple linear probes on a 70-billion-parameter model caught 95 to 99 percent of deceptive responses at a 1 percent false-positive rate, in tests that included deliberate underperformance on safety evaluations. That matters for control too: its evaluations depend on knowing what a model can really do, and sandbagging is how a schemer would hide it. An activation monitor sees what an output monitor cannot.

The honest cost: the field is young. The probe authors say theirs are not yet a robust defence; the field's roadmap lists many open problems to solve before the benefits arrive. Finding nothing in the weights is not yet proof that nothing is there. That is the case for the push, not against it. Control already shows gains on today's models; interpretability is held back by unsolved science, where serious effort changes what is possible. Only interpretability can tell us whether the model in the box is trying to get out.
